newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish watchdog proposes changes to merger rules.
newsitem.headline: Irish watchdog proposes changes to merger rules.

text.p: Ireland's Competition Authority said on Tuesday it was proposing changes to merger rules in an effort to increase transparency and efficiency in the review process.
Among its proposals, the watchdog suggested that mergers involving firms above a certain size be handled by an independent agency rather than the Minister for Enterprise and Employment.
The agency would have 30 days to decide whether the deal raised any competition concerns, and it could conduct a more detailed second-stage review if necessary.
Following this second review, the agency would give a recommendation on the merger to the minister, who would, as now, make the final decision on the deal.
The Competition Authority said this proposal would have an advantage over the current system because the same agency would deal with both stages of the process.
Under current rules, the Department of Enterprise conducts the initial examination, with the second-stage analysis done by the Competition Authority.
The watchdog said the proposal was one of its more radical alternatives submitted to the Mergers Review Group, which is considering merger legislation.

"Steps should be taken to improve the effectiveness and efficiency, promote greater transparency, reduce the cost to business and ensure that competition concerns are fully taken into account in the assessment of mergers notified under the Mergers Act," the authority said in a statement.
